name: Kodiak 100
summary: Rugged single-engine STOL utility turboprop popular with bush, mission and float operators.

wings: High-mounted, strut-braced wing with drooped leading-edge cuffs
engines: Single PT6A turboprop in a short, deep nose with a large four-blade prop
fuselage: Tall fixed tricycle gear giving a high stance
Large rear cargo door and large windows
tail: Big tall fin with a straight leading edge and a long dorsal fillet

tellTales: Stubby single turboprop on tall fixed gear with a strut-braced high wing
Four-blade prop on a short, deep nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The Kodiak is shorter and stubbier with a taller stance and bigger tail; the Caravan is long and boxy, often with a belly cargo pod.
The Kodiak is larger with a turboprop nose and a four-blade prop; the 206 is a piston single with a smaller tail.
The Kodiak has a strut-braced high wing and fixed gear; the PC-12 has a low wing, retractable gear and a T-tail.
The Porter is a tailwheel aircraft with a long, tapering nose; the Kodiak has fixed tricycle gear and a short, deep nose.
The Otter has a big round radial nose and a tailwheel or floats; the Kodiak has a turboprop nose and tricycle gear.
The Kodiak has a turbine nose and a big three-blade propeller; the GippsAero GA8 has a flat-six cowl and a smaller prop.
